ns2:section.sectionText: This seminar takes up the role of context in rhetorical research. Notions of context play a foundational role in rhetorical scholarship. Yet context itself has served, as Charles Morris and Kendall Phillips put it, as "rather a silent partner, presumed and to varying degrees practiced but not theorized, not an articulated methodological issue." Our goal in the course will be to explore historical approaches to context and to map contemporary ways that scholars place rhetoric in context. Topics and concepts we will take up include the text-context relationship, rhetorical situation, intertextuality, panhistoriography, social knowledge, form and genre, rhetorical biography, the archive, circulation studies, and rhetorical/performative traditions.
